text:
Los Angeles walks into Boston winless in four and outscored 16-6 over that stretch, and the frustrating part for the Kings is how little of it they earned. They took 54% of the expected goals (the quality of the chances each side creates) in those four losses. The season reads the same way: a minus-14 goal difference on chances that say they should be a little ahead, with 7.5 goals lost to poor finishing and 8.9 more to the goaltending. Darcy Kuemper, who reached 500 NHL games against the Islanders last week, starts again at .873 and minus-7.6 goals saved above expected. At 12 points, our simulations give the Kings a 23% playoff chance, and time is not on their side.

They are short a star, too. Artemi Panarin, 19 points in 17 games, is away for personal reasons, with ESPN estimating a Nov. 19 return. Alex Turcotte has moved up beside Alex Laferriere and Adrian Kempe, and Brandt Clarke has taken Panarin's spot on the first power-play unit. The lift is Kevin Fiala, back last week nine months after the injury he suffered at the Olympics, and now one assist from 300 for his career.

Boston is the mirror image: 27 points and a plus-19 goal difference built on chances that are only slightly better than even. Finishing (6.2 goals above the chances) and goaltending (10.5 saved above expected) do the lifting, and Michael DiPietro gets the net tonight with a .924 save percentage and plus-4.9 in six games, a long-waited chance he has grabbed. The mood is less sunny than the record. Audacy ran a headline on David Pastrnak calling the team's start "UNACCEPTABLE," and the Bruins then lost at home to Montreal and 6-2 to Minnesota. James Hagens (back) is on injured reserve; Marat Khusnutdinov has taken his spot beside Elias Lindholm and Casey Mittelstadt.

Our numbers have it close, 3.13 expected goals for Boston to 2.94. The matchup to watch is special teams: a Kings power play worth 0.77 expected goals a game against a Bruins team that takes five penalties a night.
headline: The Kings keep losing games they control
